newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee treads water, quietly up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee treads water, quietly up.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures were barely traded and prices ended Thursday midsession slightly up as activity quietened down ahead of the long U.S. weekend and eroding fears of a cold front in Brazil's coffee belt over the weekend.
Traders said light roaster buying firmed values up. Jobber activity also contributed to the small volume of 843 lots.
September traded from between $1,841 and $1,855 to finish the morning session $10 higher at $1,850. November also stood $14 higher at $1,839.
There were no fresh fundamental news. Traders said news Brazil's Santos administrative port workers to end their strike was unlikely to have any influence on the market.
The New York arabica futures posted moderate losses on Wednesday, pressured by an absence of damaging cold in Brazil and signs of a build-up in the U.S. stockpile.

"On the negative side is the jump in coffee potentially availalbe on the CSCE (the New York market) almost enough to wipe out the remnants of the open interest, and certainly enough to push prices," broker GNI said in a commentary.
No forecast is predicting any real frost risk in Brazil for the next seven days.
The New York market is closed on Friday for a local holiday. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
